name: writematrix
signature:
writematrix(A, filename)
writematrix(A, filename, Name, Value)
summary: Writes a numeric or logical matrix to a delimited text file, one row per line.
doc: The file is `.txt`, `.dat` or `.csv` (no extension adds `.txt`). Values are comma-separated unless `'Delimiter'` is `'space'`, `'tab'`, `'semi'` or `'bar'`. Numbers are written in long g format (15 significant digits; single, 7), with `NaN`, `Inf`, `-Inf` and `-0` as written. `'WriteMode', 'append'` adds to the end of the file. An array with more than two dimensions is written with its trailing dimensions collapsed into columns.
differs: The file name is required: writematrix(A), which names the file after the variable, is refused.
Spreadsheet files (.xls, .xlsx) are refused; write a .csv file.
Only numeric and logical arrays: char, string, cell and complex values are refused.
Of the options, only Delimiter, WriteMode and FileType ('text') are supported.

name: readmatrix
signature:
A = readmatrix(filename)
A = readmatrix(filename, Name, Value)
summary: Reads the numbers of a delimited text file as a matrix.
doc: The delimiter (comma, tab, semicolon, bar or spaces) and the header lines (leading lines that are not mostly numbers) are found when not given. An empty or non-numeric field is NaN (a comma inside a number is not a thousands separator: `1,5` is NaN), double-quoted fields may hold the delimiter, and a short row is padded with NaN. Options: `'Delimiter'`, `'NumHeaderLines'` and `'OutputType'` (numeric classes; NaN is 0 in an integer class).
differs: Spreadsheet files are refused; save the sheet as a .csv file.
Of the options, only Delimiter, NumHeaderLines and OutputType (numeric classes) are supported.
The header and delimiter detection is a simple heuristic, not MATLAB's.

name: fread
signature:
A = fread(fileID)
A = fread(fileID, sizeA, precision, skip, machinefmt)
[A, count] = fread(___)
summary: Reads binary data from a file opened with fopen.
doc: `sizeA` is `Inf` (a column of all that is left, the default), `n`, `[m n]` or `[m Inf]`; a partial last column is padded with zeros. `precision` is `'uint8'` (the default), `'int16'`, `'double'`, ...: it reads into double, `'*int16'` keeps the class, and `'int16=>single'` converts. `'char'` reads UTF-8 characters. The machine format (or fopen's) can be `'ieee-be'`.

examples.code:
f = fopen('b.bin', 'w'); fwrite(f, [1 2 300], 'uint16'); fclose(f);
f = fopen('b.bin'); [A, n] = fread(f, Inf, 'uint16'), fclose(f);

name: fwrite
signature:
count = fwrite(fileID, A)
count = fwrite(fileID, A, precision, skip, machinefmt)
summary: Writes an array's elements to a file in binary, in column order.
doc: `precision` is `'uint8'` by default; an integer precision rounds and saturates, as MATLAB's does. The machine format (or fopen's) can be `'ieee-be'`.

examples.code:
f = fopen('w.bin', 'w'); n = fwrite(f, [1.5 300 -2], 'uint8'), fclose(f);
f = fopen('w.bin'); fread(f)', fclose(f);
